CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidney stones

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents for evaluation of kidney stone discovered approximately one week ago. One week prior to presentation, patient developed sudden onset right-sided back pain while working in a barn moving hay. Initially attributed pain to physical exertion, but developed associated diaphoresis and nausea, prompting evaluation by his primary care physician. CT scan confirmed presence of kidney stone. This is the patient's first kidney stone. Pain radiated almost to the groin region. Since onset, patient reports minimal continued pain with brief episodes following diagnosis. Patient has been straining urine as instructed and reports no visible stone fragments. Denies hematuria. Denies dark or discolored urine.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Father with history of multiple kidney stones.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works with horses in a barn, performing work involving moving hay.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs stable with no fever. Blood pressure and heart rate normal. Abdominal examination reveals no tenderness to palpation, no rebound tenderness, and no guarding. Right costovertebral angle tenderness present.

RESULTS
CT scan demonstrates a stone measuring 0.5 centimeters located in the proximal right ureter. No evidence of hydronephrosis or ureteral obstruction. Pending laboratory studies include basic metabolic panel, urinalysis, and urine culture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Nephrolithiasis, right proximal ureteral stone (0.5 cm). Plan: encourage increased fluid intake to facilitate stone passage, oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours for pain control, acetaminophen for breakthrough pain, and continue urine straining. Obtain basic metabolic panel, urinalysis, and urine culture; prescribe antibiotics if infection identified based on urinalysis. Follow-up appointment in 1-2 weeks. If stone has not passed at that time, extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy will be discussed.
